questions.q: What is the developmental stage of a human offspring called from the ninth week of pregnancy until birth?
a: A zygote
An embryo
A fetus
A gamete

questions.q: Through which structure does the fetus receive oxygen and nutrients from the mother's blood?
a: The amniotic sac
The sperm duct
The placenta
The cervix

questions.q: What is the function of the umbilical cord?
a: To produce amniotic fluid for cushion
To connect the fetus to the placenta, transporting blood containing nutrients and waste
To act as a hard shell protecting against impact
To pump blood independently using its own small heart

questions.q: How does oxygen pass from the mother's blood into the fetal blood within the placenta?
a: By active pumping of white blood cells
By direct mixing of maternal and fetal blood streams
By diffusion across the very thin walls separating their blood supplies
By electrical attraction of red blood cells

questions.q: What is the protective fluid-filled sac that surrounds and cushions the developing fetus called?
a: The uterus
The oviduct
The amniotic sac
The ovary

questions.q: What is the primary role of the amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus?
a: To provide high amounts of starch and protein food directly
To digest waste products produced by the baby
To protect the fetus from physical shocks and bumps while allowing movement
To act as the primary site for gas exchange

questions.q: Which waste substance produced by fetal cellular respiration diffuses across the placenta into the mother's blood to be excreted?
a: Oxygen
Glucose
Carbon dioxide
Amino acids

questions.q: Approximately how long does normal human gestation (fetal development inside the womb) last?
a: About 3 weeks
About 6 months
About 2 years
About 9 months (40 weeks)

questions.q: Which harmful substance, if consumed by a pregnant woman, can cross the placenta and restrict oxygen delivery to the fetus, leading to low birth weight?
a: Pure mineral water
Dietary calcium
Nicotine from tobacco smoke
Plant cellulose fiber

questions.q: What happens to the waste urea produced by the fetus?
a: It builds up inside the baby permanently
It turns into solid bone tissue
It diffuses across the placenta into the mother's blood so her kidneys can remove it
It is exhaled directly through the baby's lungs

questions.q: Which major organs begin to form and become functional during the first trimester before the fetal stage begins?
a: Permanent adult teeth
The heart, brain, and main spinal cord
Hair follicles and facial beard
Knee and elbow cartilage

questions.q: Why is it important that maternal and fetal blood do not physically mix together in the placenta?
a: Because fetal blood is solid and cannot flow
To prevent the baby from breathing air too early
To protect the fetus from different blood group reactions and high maternal blood pressure
So the mother can store extra blood

questions.q: What term describes the period of time when a baby develops inside the mother's uterus prior to birth?
a: Menstruation
Ovulation
Pollination
Gestation

questions.q: During which part of pregnancy is the developing organism most vulnerable to damage from harmful chemicals, alcohol, and infections?
a: The final week before birth
During childhood growth
After the umbilical cord is cut
The early embryonic and first trimester stages when major organs are forming

questions.q: What is the main source of glucose and amino acids for a growing fetus?
a: Swallowing amniotic fluid directly as solid meals
Transfer from the mother's blood through the placenta
Direct sunlight shining through the womb
Ingesting food from the amniotic sac

questions.q: What happens to the amniotic sac and fluid just before a baby is born?
a: It seals permanently to store more fluid
It turns into solid bone
It is absorbed completely into the mother's stomach
It ruptures, releasing the fluid through the vagina (commonly known as 'water breaking')

questions.q: Which of the following describes the fetus near the end of the third trimester?
a: A single unfertilized egg cell
A hollow ball of identical stem cells
A microscopic zygote dividing for the first time
Fully formed with developed organs, putting on weight, and ready for birth

questions.q: How does alcohol consumed by a pregnant mother affect the developing fetus?
a: It helps the fetus grow stronger bones
It provides extra vitamins for brain growth
It has no effect on the fetus whatsoever
It can cross the placenta, causing developmental delays and fetal alcohol syndrome

questions.q: What is the role of the muscular walls of the uterus during the final stage of pregnancy (labor)?
a: To relax completely and stop all blood flow
To digest the placenta internally
To produce milk before birth
To contract rhythmically with strong force to push the baby out through the cervix and vagina

questions.q: What happens immediately after the baby is born and the umbilical cord is clamped and cut?
a: The baby stops all metabolic activity
The mother's body shuts down completely
The fetus turns back into an embryo
The baby's lungs take in air for the first time, and independent breathing and circulation begin

questions.q: Which nutrients are stored in the fetus's body during the final weeks of gestation to provide energy after birth before feeding starts?
a: Pure iron metal chunks
Fats (adipose tissue) and glycogen
Calcium carbonate rocks
Cellulose fiber layers

questions.q: What structural feature of the placenta maximizes the rate of diffusion between mother and baby?
a: A thick layer of muscle and bone
Rigid cartilage rings preventing expansion
A massive surface area with extremely thin barrier walls
Active hydraulic pumps

questions.q: Why is the fetus unable to use its lungs to breathe air while inside the uterus?
a: Because the baby holds its breath for 9 months
Because the lungs are filled with amniotic fluid and gas exchange is handled entirely by the placenta
Because the mother has no oxygen in her blood
Because the trachea is tied in a knot

questions.q: What is the transition stage between a single-celled zygote and an established fetus called?
a: The adult stage
The menopausal stage
The geriatric stage
The embryonic stage

questions.q: How do infectious pathogens like certain viruses sometimes affect a fetus?
a: They strengthen the baby's immune system permanently
They turn into harmless protein food
They can cross the placenta barrier and disrupt normal organ development
They are blocked completely with 100 percent efficiency under all circumstances

questions.q: What role does the hormone progesterone play during gestation?
a: It causes the uterine lining to break down immediately
It induces rapid muscle fatigue
It triggers the onset of puberty
It maintains and thickens the lining of the uterus and prevents menstruation during pregnancy

questions.q: What is the medical term for giving birth to the baby?
a: Ovulation
Implantation
Fertilization
Parturition (labor and birth)

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding the heart of a developing fetus?
a: It only begins beating after the baby is born
It is replaced by a mechanical pump inside the womb
It starts beating weeks before birth during early development
It pumps blood that mixes directly with the mother's heart

questions.q: What happens to the placenta after the baby is delivered?
a: It remains inside the mother permanently as an organ
It turns into milk-producing mammary glands
It travels up into the baby's abdomen
It is expelled from the uterus shortly after birth as the 'afterbirth'

questions.q: Why do pregnant women require extra dietary iron and folic acid?
a: To prevent tooth decay in their own mouth
To support increased blood volume, placenta growth, and neural tube development in the fetus
To increase their physical height
To digest fats without bile

questions.q: What protects the fetus from loud external sounds and bright lights?
a: A thick layer of steel armor
Special sunglasses and earplugs worn inside the womb
Complete darkness and silence inside the mother's body at all times
The mother's abdominal muscles, uterine wall, amniotic fluid, and membranes

questions.q: At roughly what point in pregnancy can the heartbeat of a fetus typically be detected using specialized equipment like an ultrasound?
a: Only on the exact day of birth
During the first trimester (around weeks 6 to 12)
During the teenage years
Never before birth

questions.q: What is the main function of the umbilical vein within the umbilical cord?
a: To carry waste-laden blood away from the fetus
To carry oxygen-rich and nutrient-rich blood from the placenta to the fetus
To pump amniotic fluid into the stomach
To connect the baby's lungs directly to the mother's lungs

questions.q: What is the main function of the two umbilical arteries within the umbilical cord?
a: To supply fresh oxygen directly to the brain
To feed the placenta with maternal food
To circulate milk inside the fetus
To carry deoxygenated blood and metabolic waste away from the fetus toward the placenta

questions.q: How does temperature regulation work for a fetus inside the womb?
a: The fetus shivers to generate heat
The fetus sweats to cool down
The fetus relies entirely on the mother's internal body temperature via the placenta and amniotic fluid
The baby wears tiny thermal clothes

questions.q: What characterizes the second trimester of pregnancy (weeks 13 to 26)?
a: The initial fusion of sperm and egg
The immediate process of labor and birth
The cessation of all organ development
Rapid growth in size, bone development, and the mother starting to feel fetal movements (quickening)

questions.q: Why is smoking during pregnancy linked to lower birth weights in babies?
a: Smoking makes the mother eat less food
Carbon monoxide binds to hemoglobin instead of oxygen, reducing oxygen delivery required for fetal growth
Nicotine increases the baby's physical activity too much
Tobacco fibers block the digestive tract

questions.q: What happens to the cervix during labor before the baby can pass through the vagina?
a: It seals shut with solid bone
It shrinks to microscopic size
It dilates (widens) significantly to allow the baby's head and body to pass through
It detaches completely from the body

questions.q: Which medical scan is commonly used during pregnancy to monitor fetal growth, check for abnormalities, and view position?
a: X-ray fluoroscopy
Magnetic resonance thermometer
Ultrasound imaging (sonogram)
Ultraviolet light scan

questions.q: What is the term for a baby born significantly before 37 weeks of full gestation?
a: A post-term zygote
An embryonic clone
A fully mature adult
A premature (pre-term) baby
